lines: The things that try to kill me:
Flashing zippy gut splatterers,
sticky spiral graveyards,
plain old dehydration, and
a lumbering beast who guards their slop,
infuriated with me and the air around me.
They swing slowly and wide.
While jumping, while climbing.
The stench calls to me.
From lamp to cupboard to ceiling,
back to lamp and to ceiling again — hide in a shadow.
SWAT!
A lousy swing.
CRACK!
The room goes quiet.
I land on the nicest pile of shit.
A pixelated buffet begging for my barf.¹
Oh fuck! My labella ignites with pleasure.
I ate, I drank,
and in the warmth of it all,
I laid there,
no hurry, buzzing.
The swatting ended cold, and
nothing crashed against me.
A light reached out,
lured me up from the shit,
i threw myself against its warmth,
hard, and for so long I forgot why I began to try.
A pungent stench, loud as life,
the rot of the world,
stole my attention from the warmth.²
My sweets will eat a feast.
Dried up a heartbeat later,
revolting but unaware,
ready to fly around again.
Footnotes
¹ "Never keep it down, thass what I say. Get it up while it's fresh on your stomach, like." — George Orwell, 1984
² "And first he will see the shadows best, next the reflections of men and other objects in the water, and then the objects themselves…" — Plato, Allegory of the Cave
The real orgy begins after midnight
as crickets rub the ridges of their wings together.
The air is filled with white noise
like the buzzing in my ears when it's past late and I'm buried in the pillows.
A choir of crickets call to their counterparts
scattered amongst the weeds,
their siren song harping out a fuck-me chorus:
Let's do this dirty cricket dance, my love!
Let's fuck each other in the open!
Let's not give two shits about who's watching
and conceive a swarm of locusts to devour the fields!
A cat wails loudly,
piercing the night with her shrill cry.
Her resounding echo reminds me to bury my head
deeper in the down.
She tiptoes along a fencepost
peering cautiously into an empty lot.
She emboldens the tomcats with the cooing
of her promissory note
beckoning them from their foraging grounds:
Take me on this fencepost!
Take me on the lid of this garbage can!
Take me in the middle of this cold night or I'll cry into the morning!
I want to conceive eight kittens in this forsaken place!
The moon sits low above a row of twisted pines,
a spotlight igniting the knick-knacks on my dresser.
A mockingbird perched high in a tree
warbles out a lonely solo.
He sings to the wild of the night,
a desperate birdy bootycall when
he really should be sleeping:
If you're awake come over!
There's room for three or even more!
My plumage is preened and I'm full of songs I've memorized!
Come nest with me and we'll fluff each other's feathers!
A pulse of white ignites the sky
like the strike of my lighter
in the backseat of a car,
a brief intermission
before the orgy continues.
Sunrise raindrops skydive into puddles
and bounce back out
briefly
before a final cannonball.
Shrouded in darkness,
the blankets crept
to the top of the bed,
over the head
of the innocent.
Shrouded in darkness,
the Anus expelled the fart,
filling the blanket
to its bitter brim
of capacity.
Shrouded In Darkness!
the innocent
was smothered,
snuffed out
by an Anus
and a fart.
Sometimes I have to beg the daemons
to keep their whispers to themselves
not now
not as I've finally settled down
not while I'm thinking of my dog
and the breeze is gently blowing
intently through my hair
do I have to hear your voices
can't it wait until the morning
why not when the coffee's brewing
when the bagel and the lox
are married to the schmear
Yet the past comes rolling onward
like a train without a ticket
rolling coal through autumn nights
nauseous
in the thick of it
halting cars with eager drivers
intent on lying down
once lost in calculations
now trapped behind the wheel
Alone with thoughts again
I should've pushed my chances
before the guard came down
a joyride magnum opus
I've never seen it in the real
no doubt I'd feel the rapture
at worst I'd be derailed
either way I'd make it home
far from the other side
I could be half way there now
cuddled with my dog
this is a haiku
about a fucking lost cat
where you at kitty
SweetPea my darling
you precious little ho bag
i've got a question
where the fuck are you
if you are somewhere nearby
please give me a sign
meow meow meow meow meow
meow meow meow meow meow meow meow
meow meow meow meow meow
There's a zen meditation center in my little town,
and I joined a metta session this afternoon.
The monk is sweet and invites the community to join
(or to just come and go or do whatever),
and some people take advantage of that.
A group of people came in for the coffee and snacks
and had a side conversation in the room during the meditation.
Most of it was incomprehensible, but some of it was loud enough to make out.
For instance, one of them was describing a person he knew
who could catch arrows in mid flight.
I felt myself getting annoyed,
but I also had a funny revelation.
I've meditated outside before,
and the birds were chirping much more
than these people were talking.
I thought,
what if I knew what the birds were saying?
i love sunshine.
i'm going to miss her while she's gone.
i'll think of her periodically because
i'll see someone standing on their hands.
i'll call her and leave a message
and i hope she smiles when she hears it.
i hope she has a great trip and learns a lot
and makes a lot of people fall in love with her
and falls in love a couple times, too
and experiences nature in a new way
or at least comes to some new way of thinking about nature.
i hope she eats something exotic.
i love sunshine.
i'm going to miss her while she's gone.
I'm a goliath in a world of giants.
Try as I can it's simply providence
that I've not been wrenched into an experiment
of some forensic scientist who thinks I'm a ghastly cadavre.
Instead I stomp around thinking my footprints are pretty to look at,
I howl at the moon because it stalks me
and pokes fun at my fair complexion
and reminds me that the sun'll come out
tomorrow.
i eat the locals.
I make pots of boiling water
and line them up in two by twos.
I drop them into my human au jus.
Their screams are simply air escaping
and their dreams are simply retards playing.
The women taste the best
since their bones make a special crunch.
The men are a sordid bunch,
but their tough-guy personas make for a tastey brunch.
Dragons at creationist camp.
They're basically saying that because some ancient cultures
in Asia and Africa have mythical tales about flying beasts that spew fire,
then the dinosaurs lived at the same time as humans, proving Creationism.
They discount scientific claims that dinosaurs went extinct millions of years ago
because these myths about dragons exist,
and they believe the dragons are actually dinosaurs,
proving that humans and dinosaurs lived at the same time,
which proves the universe was created by God.
It seems there is a line of logic
anyone can create cognitively
in order to continue believing in something
no matter what.
Flying at super-sonic speeds,
it's hard for anyone to see them.
It's even harder to imagine
just how anyone could beat them.
Machines, Machines, Machines
are Fighting for our Freedom.
While kids are herding goats,
a mother goes out to meet them.
But instead of finding children,
she finds a missile there to greet them.
Machines, Machines, Machines
are Fighting for our Freedom.
Bible and flag in his hand,
the politician swears that we need them.
"They're fast, they're effective,
and we don't even have to feed them!"
Machines, Machines, Machines
are Fighting for our Freedom.
Soldiers' names sound so noble
when they're dead and politicians read them.
"Have no fear, we'll bring them home,
the machine is always here to lead them!"
Machines, Machines, Machines
are Fighting for our Freedom.
Someone asked me what I get out of life.
"an interesting story to tell."
They pried and asked what the story is about.
"a kid who goes out in search of Graceland,
or the mothership, or something."
Does the kid find the mothership?
"no, he turns around and goes back home."
Why did he stop searching?
"he didn't stop searching,
he started looking somewhere else."
You
should know,
I dream of you naked,
thrashing on a bed of roses.
Are you smelling all the flowers?
Are you bleeding from all the thistles?
Are you planted with the bushes in the dirt?
Your smile is borne by your haunting gaze,
your hair is terra cotta.
Your bangs fall uneven across your face,
chaotic as if chopped with a hatchet.
Your eyes are baked crockeries formed from china clay,
your irises crystal glazed celadon.
Art is on your hands, on your fingertips.
Torn from forming, scabbed from mourning,
your hands become the art your art creates:
mended fabric, sewn and worn,
canvas brushed and spattered, cupcakes iced and sprinkled.
Your fingers are figures painted naked and shameless,
sometimes serious, sometimes playful.
Your freckles are constellations
used to navigate the body;
vessels are charting,
disregarding
the jagged
rocks.
I'm sorry
Bukowski
but sometimes the poem doesn't burst forth like you said it should.
Sometimes it only leaks out
like a faucet
an annoying drip
at 3am.
And I have to decide if it's worth it
to get up and turn the nozzle
or roll over
and keep dreaming
about that time I left my shotgun in the break room.
Searching for equanimity,
I tip-toed carefully around the graves
Noting the names of those
Who sleep below the dirt
That, by my toes and body motion,
Is gently stirred.
I hummed softly 'til it came...
FLASH!
White lightning glowed.
One-Mississippi, Two-Mississippi
CRASH!
Then down below
The ground was thrashed to and fro.
Yippee!
I asked for rain and now, by Jove
I've got it!
The sky, dark and disarranged,
Slowly freed the water resting at its gates.
It was time to decide.
I closed my eyes.
I doffed my clothes
I showered in the rain.*
Soap in hand I ran,
Naked, like any other man.
I was watered down,
I was soaked, yet without shame.
With no disguise I hustled;
Quickstepping across a street
Shimmying down an ally
Twisting around a corner
Stomping up a hill
limboing beneath lit windows.
Reeling, I stood in a field where
A far off lamp was revealed and
With a loco motion I made my way;
I arrived at the lamp by cakewalk,
by foxtrot,
by paso doble.
Standing in the fashion you'd expect it to stand, the lamp
Resided on a bridge painted sarcastically
With a mural of kid's names
Sprayed in the most splendid of ways.
The ground was broken glass and fishing string,
Discarded bait and other things that
People leave behind when rain-clouds gather.
Their rainy day, my play date.
I lathered my hands, and under the lamp
I scrubbed away my inhibitions.
I was sudded up from head to butt
When a dump truck driver sped clumsily up,
And passed without a wink or even a slight wave.
He would have seen me if not for his task
Of tilting back black cans,
Gathering together the cities white trash.
I stared back at the street lamp,
And at my cold breath that, for a second,
Clouded the view.
The light was significant, I felt invisible.
A damp, yellow luminescence
oil on a black and purple canvas.
I was painted.†
The light ruled the moment,
And no one ruled the light.
Now the rain was pouring down
Hard, on my crown and brow
And back and frown, and on
My hands and toes
And skin and bones,
So I began to dance.
I spun around with my arms aimed out
I howled loud
Teach Me Something!
The raindrops were first to answer.
I listened closely to every plop.
With my footfall timed to every drop.
Shivering I waltzed,
One big step,          two small steps,
Daa-  da-  da,         Daa-  da-  da
Until the splattering clops deafened my thoughts
And I was convinced that my trot was taking me not
Forward, but back
To a better dance‡
When someone wanted my hand.
To be held and missed
To be spun and dipped, funned and kissed.
I danced through the night to the sound of the rain like
Nails striking the tops of tin-cans.
With my eyes closed I waltzed with my friend.
Holding her tight at trunk and palm,
No one led, we both followed.
We waltzed through knee deep puddles,
On top of speed bumps and down the middle lane.
I spun her round and she laughed aloud
But when I leaned in,
She bowed out.
I knew in that moment,
The rain had nothing it could teach me.
The dump truck driver came by again.
This time, much slower.
He was old; enough so when he cranked his neck
His jaw was forced to lower.
"A naked man! Covered in soap!
Dancing alone in the rain at two in the morning!"
He was a good man, that driver.
He wanted to stop, to ask if I was okay.
But, not wanting to intrude, he let me dance.
Again I started trembling,
Despite my constant stepping.
One big one, two small ones,
Daa-da-da, Daa-da-da.
I decided to do something else.
Instead,
I'll teach myself
Since the rain won't help.
I thought to lie in the road
With my mouth agape and wait
Until
it
was
full
and swallow the pool.
I thought to climb a tree and jump
Down
into a puddle, or run
And skip in giant bounds,
Hovering for a second
Over the ground.
And slowly,
Eventually
Float
ing
do
w
n
and then
Rebounding
And Pouncing
Back to the peak
Of the previous leap
Hovering for a second
Over the ground
Until gravity
Once again
Drags
Me
Do
w
n
I
know
now
I
can
re
bound.
but will i remember
The choice that is difficult to choose,
The lesson that is easy to lose:
Whether or not to dance,
And, weather or not,
To continue.
Footnotes
* "What we do is in our genes, we're simply trying to disguise it."
† "The trials we face are manifestations of character."
‡ "Anticipation may provide more happiness than actually getting the thing we want."
The protagonist (X) is a manic-depressive who has experienced suicidal thoughts for most of his life. He practices meditation, but all it has served to do is create space
between him and the suicidal scenarios he imagines every day. As if he were watching a movie of himself committing suicide. Being aware of the thoughts is advantageous in
that at least nowadays the movies are in the third-person. X lives an average suburban life tinged with the curse of procrastination and ADD. His cluttered apartment and
failing health are evidence of his pathetic stage in life. In a conversation with his best friend and roommate (Y) he describes an idea wherein he plans his own suicide and
uses the money from the life insurance to throw a banger for all his friends and family.
A few weeks later, Y kills himself, and in the will he leaves instructions for his life insurance money to be spent on an elaborate and intricately planned wake. X is surprised
and confused and a little hurt that his friend stole his idea. X tells his girlfriend that he's a little upset at Y for taking his idea. She blames him for planting the idea in Y's mind
and breaks up with him, "I'm tired of this boring roller coaster."
Y's idea goes viral on social media. Thousands of people kill themselves in the coming week, and one-upmanship ensues.
At Y's wake, X catches up with the myriad attendees including some old friends (A, B, & C) he hadn't seen in a long time. X strikes up awkward conversations regarding suicide
and the ethos of celebrating it. A says he deals with this shit by dropping acid and gives some to X. X sees his ex-girlfriend at the wake with a new person and tries to ignore
them by taking the acid. Y's friends and family have a cathartic experience as the wake plays out highlights and reveals secrets from Y's life. Overwhelmed, X spends the night
in the janitor's closet amused by the simple things.
As society is gripped by the trend, celebrities begin to appropriate it. Shenanigans.
Inspired by society's new, relaxed stance on suicide, and in order to fully understand Y's decision, X decides to follow through with his incessant thoughts and kill himself. As
he begins to layout the plans for his own wake, X realizes he lacks any motivation to make the plans. A simple Internet search reveals Suicide Party.
Suicide Party is a startup company that offers to plan your wake for you. SP is funded by health and life insurance companies who have calculated that it would be cheaper to
pay the life insurance policies of people than pay their health insurance bills.
The automated process for making an account has not yet been completed, so an in-person interview is scheduled. X is required to bring certain documents and affects to
help establish the legality as well as the plans. Procrastination takes hold again and he throws together a makeshift box of trinkets to bring to the meeting.
X arrives at a shabby "office" and meets Z, a scatter-brained multi-tasker and the founder and CEO of SP. There is an initial attraction, but professionalism quickly prevails and
they get down to business. They go through the paperwork and X begins to make the connection about the healthcare/life insurance companies' scheme. X is distracted by the
lies he finds himself weaving for the random items he brought to inspire his wake. Z seems charmed by some of the weird things. They set a tentative date for the suicide. Z
has one client ahead of X, and says they'll be in touch soon in order to finesse the details.
X wakes up the next day and feels great. He picks up a book and begins reading it, something he'd been unable to manage for years. He cooks a splendid lunch, goes for a
charming walk, and takes a glorious shower. He decides to call A, B, & C, the friends he reconnected with at Y's wake, and they all meet up for drinks that night. They note X's
chipper demeanor. X sees Z at a table with a group of friends and they share distant greetings. C reveals that they are planning their own wake through a company called
"immOURlation," but they can't decide on the details surrounding how to actually die. B recommends a company he's been researching called "YOUicide" since they have so
many more options. X becomes indignant, asking what B or C could possibly be depressed about that they might kill themselves. C is offended, reminding X "the divorce was a
really painful experience." X is befuddled, "you're still engaged!" C is referring to his parents' divorce. B says he wants to die because he can't stop smoking and doesn't want to
die of cancer. X is quite drunk by this time and is pointing out all the good things his friends have. It comes across as condescending, and A rises to his friends' defense. X and
A have a fist fight, landing A in the hospital and X in jail.
On the TV in jail, X sees a snippet from the news. People are now throwing parties in which everyone at the party commits suicide together, and in turn they have wakes of
their own wherein everyone who goes to that wake commits suicide together.
X's brother posts bail. They haven't talked in ages. "Yours is the only number I know by heart besides JG Wentworth." "Oh, you've got jokes now? Being a criminal has loosened
you up, huh?" X feels bad for hurting his friend, but does feel a strange sense of glory and freedom in the experience. He's lost his job, bills are past due, electricity is turned
off, is estranged from his friends (again), and he has a court date for assault and battery.
After charging his phone at a nearby hotel's free continental breakfast, X notices a voicemail from Z at Suicide Party; "I saw you in that fight at the bar. Is the guy who tripped
on the bar stool okay? Why did you get arrested? BTW, convicted felons are not allowed to use the services of SP. I hope everything is okay!"
This happens, and therefore this happens, but this happens, therefore this happens.
August 3, 2013:
I packed some grapes and a few cookies in my cargo pockets and took the bus to the Walmart where I intended to investigate what the radio called "the best contraceptive
ever!" This "contraceptive" is a pair of stockings that make a woman's legs look like they are covered in thick, coarse hair. They are definitely not a contraceptive, but are
intended to keep weirdos and perverts at bay. Don't girls know that the most perverted weirdos prefer hairy legs?
As I walked through the parking lot, I noticed a woman parking in the "expectant mother" spot. I thought, does that mean anyone who is expecting to have a child one day is
allowed to park there? No, that is not the case; the spot is only for those who are currently pregnant.
The woman parked her car and walked ahead of me into Walmart. She was heavyset with red hair and extensive freckles, as if someone threw mud at her through a screen
door. Her pants were tight on her hips and I could make out the shape of her panties: they were "grandmother" panties.
I thought, what if she isn't pregnant? What if she is only fat? That's not for me to judge so I decided to let it go. But as we entered the store, she walked in the same direction as
me, towards the "female products".
I am only looking for stockings covered in thick hair to see if they are real and if they come in different colors for girls with different colored hair, and to see what ingredients
are used to make the hair; are they made with real hair? I am not following the "pregnant woman".
She turns down an aisle and I walk past her to the "feminine garments" section of the store. I find the isle where stockings and pantyhose are stocked. I do not see any
stockings with hair. I can't ask for assistance because nobody at Walmart ever shows you where something is, they just point and say it's on the isle where you were a minute
ago.
I walk around to see if they are stocked on an end cap, and I see the "pregnant woman" looking at some panties that my grandmother would never wear. She might know about
the stockings, so I walk towards her, but before I have a chance to ask my question, I am caught by the contents of her little Walmart basket: tampons! (Pregnant women do
not use tampons because they do not have a period because a sperm fertilized their egg, and although some women do experience vaginal bleeding during pregnancy, they
would never use tampons to stop the bleeding because of the possibility of Toxic Shock Syndrome, which sounds terrifying)
I asked her, "Are you menstruating?" She seemed toxically shocked by the question at first, but after a few seconds she reluctantly answered and said, "yes, why do you ask?"
"That means you aren't pregnant!" I exclaimed. She patted me on the head and said, "that's right, but the lord knows I am trying." I hate being patted on the head.
"Well, you shouldn't've parked in the expectant mother spot if you are not pregnant."
She was silent for a few more seconds. "Excuse me? Expectant mother spot?" Yes, I saw you park in the expectant mother parking spot. Pregnancy is a very serious condition. I
won't report you this time, but next time, you better believe I will."
She knelt down and she exhaled a little grunt, which means it was not easy for her to bend down that low. She put her face very close to mine and said, "next time, I will be
pregnant."
She grunted again as she stood and put the non-grandmother panties in her basket, and then she walked away.
I wish I would've asked her where the hairy stockings were before I asked her if she was menstruating.
You bite your nails to the skin and let your leg hair grow
i say you might be doing it backwards, love
But what the hell do I know
I don't know much about a lot,
and even less about the rest,
I know if you leave before I do,
I'll keep some of your ashes.
I imagine that you'd love it if I sprinkled you in the garden.
I'll only save a little,
I want to breathe them in,
I'll want to touch and feel your grit,
View you beneath a microscope,
and even taste a bit.
I love you now and I loved you then,
I'll love you after its all over,
and when it starts again.
i'm growing old and that's alright
i'll see you soon, to all goodnight
i'm going back to when
I loved my country and you loved your cat
True love meant you could fart out loud
you could burp when you really want
and i'd tell you honey i was proud
right in the middle of the rest'rant
You'd look at me and gimme that grin
And i'd tell you you weren't fat
Our love was free like the wind
back when
I loved my country and you loved your cat
but life goes so fast and some finish last
and i guess that i'm okay with that
so long as
I love my country and you love your cat.
One day when i was playing outside
a thought popped into my mind
what if i threw dirt on my brother's food
i wonder what he would do
i grabbed some sand and brought it inside
and found a place for me to hide
when he wasn't looking i dropped it in his soup
he took one bite and then he knew
i tried to run but he kicked me on the ass
my mom looked up as i flew past
i flipped through the air and landed on my caboose,
now i don't throw dirt in people's soup.
when i was a kid i was a little puke
i threw dirt in peoples soup
kids don't need a reason why
we're trying hard just to get by
Another day when i was playing outside
a thought popped into my mind
what if i told my brother to eat some ants
would he do what his brother commands?
i told him when i'm feeling hungry
i eat ants just like a monkey
i said to him, here is the goal
and i pretended to swallow one whole
he said now let me have a go
and then an ant bit him in the throat
he looked like he was in a trance
now i don't tell people to eat ants.
